More upper 90s ahead this week
EVANSVILLE, Ind. (WFIE) -Saturday’s temperature surged to 102 at Evansville Regional Airport, the highest temp since 2012 and the second-hottest September day on record. September 5, 1953 still holds the record with 103. The intense heat is on hold for Sunday and Monday. Highs will stay in the lower 90s with lower humidity. Another spike in the upper 90s will arrive by the middle of the week.
Early clouds on Sunday will give way to mostly sunny skies by the afternoon. Northeasterly winds will send less-humid air into the Tri-State to keep the heat index in check through Labor Day. Normal highs are in the middle 80s, so we will still be warmer than normal for the holiday.
Southerly winds return on Tuesday. The humid, tropical air will sweep back in and send temperatures into the mid to upper 90s each day. Heat index values will likely climb into the triple-digits in the 105-110 degree range.
Active weather arrives with a cold front late Wednesday through early Friday. Scattered showers and storms are likely and temps will finally get knocked down into the middle 80s. Beneficial rain is possible with some models showing a half-inch or more with the thunderstorms.
